proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
p=\frac{k+1}{k+m+1},
\qquad
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}.
\]
By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\), the models used in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:localized\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\) belong to the fixed class. That theorem therefore supplies constants \(c>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{low}}>0\), depending only on the fixed class constants and on the fixed dimension, such that
\[
\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)
\geq c\varepsilon^p,
\qquad
0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{low}}.
\tag{1}
\]

For the upper bound, fix arbitrary \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) satisfying
\[
D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq\varepsilon.
\tag{2}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\), whose density-overlap and decoder-conditioning hypotheses are included in Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), gives a class-uniform constant \(C_{\mathrm{red}}<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C_{\mathrm{red}}D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C_{\mathrm{red}}\varepsilon.
\tag{3}
\]
Choose
\[
\varepsilon_0
\leq
\min\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{low}},C_{\mathrm{red}}^{-1}\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Then \(0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0\) implies \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq1\), which is the small-residual premise of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:scalar\text{-}finite\text{-}type\text{-}weak\text{-}rigidity}\). Applying that lemma to (3) yields
\[
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)
\leq C_{\mathrm{rig}}\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)^q
\leq C_{\mathrm{rig}}C_{\mathrm{red}}^q\varepsilon^q.
\tag{5}
\]
The pair in (2) was arbitrary. Taking the supremum in Definition \(\mathrm{def:inverse\text{-}modulus}\) and enlarging the upper constant if necessary gives
\[
\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)
\leq C\varepsilon^q,
\qquad
0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (1) and (6) proves the full-class bracket.

For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), direct substitution gives
\[
p=\frac{2+1}{2+1+1}=\frac34,
\qquad
q=\frac{2}{(2+2/2)(1+1)}=\frac13.
\tag{7}
\]
Every pair in the primary Morse class is also a pair in \(\mathcal M_{2,2,1}\), so (6) supplies its restricted upper bound. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:primary\text{-}morse\text{-}audit}\) places the localized lower family in \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\), so (1) supplies the restricted lower bound. This proves the asserted primary bracket.

Finally, suppose \(D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)=0\). Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) proves directly, from equality of the aligned complete laws and the finite-type isolated-zero conditions, that the transition map has coordinate form after one common node permutation, with every coordinate map a circle diffeomorphism. Hence the two encoders are identified up to the declared action \(\mathfrak S_n\ltimes\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb T)^n\). This implication is obtained from the direct torus identification proposition; it does not use the invalid converse inference from \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}=0\) to quotient equivalence. The same proposition separates the paired intervention conditions used for zero-law identification from the additional quantitative envelopes used in (3)--(6).

Substitute \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\) into Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}full\text{-}modulus}\). Its two exponents become
\[
\frac{k+1}{k+m+1}=\frac34,
\qquad
\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}=\frac13,
\]
and therefore, for sufficiently small positive \(\varepsilon\),
\[
c\varepsilon^{3/4}
\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)
\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is a bracket, not a claim that the full modulus has been shown to be of exact order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\). Independently, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:radial\text{-}subclass\text{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
\Omega_{2,1}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)
\asymp
\varepsilon^{(2+1)/(2+1+1)}
=\varepsilon^{3/4},
\tag{2}
\]
which is the two-sided sharp statement on the radial subclass.

If \(D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)=0\), Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) applies directly and shows that the coordinates differ by one common node permutation and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:symmetric\text{-}quotient\text{-}pseudometric}\) then gives vanishing \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) for such equivalent encoders. The logical direction used here is quotient equivalence implying zero discrepancy; no converse property of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) is invoked.

It remains to verify the plateau boundary. Suppose that a contrast \(r_{\theta i}\) is constant on a nonempty open arc \(I\subset\mathbb T\). Differentiability gives
\[
r_{\theta i}'(t)=0
\qquad (t\in I).
\]
By Definition of the critical set, \(I\subseteq Z_{\theta i}\). A nonempty open arc contains infinitely many points, whereas Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:critical\text{-}cardinality}\) requires \(|Z_{\theta i}|\leq J<\infty\). This contradiction proves that plateaus are outside the class covered by (1) and (2).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed nondegenerate bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing the lower family, there exist constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) and \(\varepsilon_0>0\) such that
\[
c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
\leq \Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)
\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}
\qquad (0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0).
\]
Here \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) is the symmetric aligned discrepancy. For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the full-class bracket has lower exponent \(3/4\) and upper exponent \(1/3\); the same bracket holds when the supremum is restricted to \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\). Whenever \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\) in the class satisfy \(D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)=0\), their torus encoders are directly identified up to one common node permutation and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms. This exact conclusion follows from Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\), while the strengthened smoothness, conditioning, separation, and attained-order hypotheses are used for the uniform nonzero-error bracket.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen scalar weak-rigidity lemma proves only the conservative exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\) for arbitrary maps. The claimed matching full-class upper exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) would require the still-open incompressible-rigidity inequality. The localized lower exponent and the direct zero-law identification remain valid.

\]

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing claim incorrectly promotes the sharp radial \(3/4\) rate to a sharp full-class rate. The proved full result is the lower exponent \(3/4\) and upper exponent \(1/3\), while the radial subclass retains its two-sided \(3/4\) frontier. Exact recovery is supplied directly by the torus identification proposition, not by a converse property of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\).

proposed.justification: The theorem gives the proved full-class inverse-modulus bracket, isolates the unresolved gap between its exponents, and separates the direct \(C^2\) Morse headline from the general finite-type rate class.

proposed.consumer: Likelihood and score-based causal representation learners obtain a certified conservative translation from complete-law error to encoder error, together with a sharp lower obstruction and a precisely isolated sharpness gap.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the unsupported matching upper claim, restore the direct exact-identification dependency, and retain the established lower and conservative upper bounds.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq\varepsilon}d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\), with the proved full-class bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\) on each fixed bounded class containing the lower family, and the proved identity \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\) case, the full bracket has lower exponent \(3/4\) and upper exponent \(1/3\), while the radial exponent is sharply \(3/4\). The matching sharp full-class upper bound remains the open question \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: Keep the headline functional coherent with the corrected full-class theorem and standardize the conservative exponent without stray punctuation.

prose_updates.tldr: Complete paired interventions yield a synthetic product law and ratio residuals. For the full bounded finite-type class, the proved inverse-modulus result is the bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\); the sharper upper exponent remains the arbitrary-map incompressible-rigidity question. The radial subclass is sharp at \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse case, this means a full-class \(3/4\) lower exponent versus a \(1/3\) upper exponent, with a sharp radial exponent \(3/4\). Zero-law componentwise circular recovery follows from the direct torus identification argument, not from a converse characterization of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\). The certified Fourier estimator and quotient confidence-set diameter inherit the conservative exponent, giving the primary rate \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).

project_justification.fill: The project proves the synthetic product reduction, a direct zero-law torus identification result, the localized full-class lower obstruction, the conservative scalar-rigidity upper bound, the exact radial frontier, and the environment-by-environment two-node Morse audit. It also gives certified Fourier recovery and symmetric quotient confidence sets at the conservative rate, while isolating arbitrary-map incompressible rigidity as the sole step needed to close the full-class exponent gap.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Positive truncated Fourier density estimation uses the vanishing floor \(\eta_N=N^{-1}\) and corrected normalization, followed by a certified finite minimum-distance fit; no derivative of an estimated density is required. The true observed densities retain the uniform lower bound \(c_0K^{-n}\). The law radius \(\rho_N\) is propagated through the proved exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), which yields \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\) in the primary case.

prose_updates.related_work: Liang et al. establish exact CauCA recovery under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one rotations on common plateaus. Varıcı et al. derive componentwise and graph recovery from exact sparse score changes under paired node interventions. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) proves the present zero-law torus conclusion directly and uses those papers only to compare assumptions and conclusion types. Neither comparator supplies a nonzero-error modulus. Buchholz and Schölkopf quantify near-isometric representation learning through a different primitive defect. Khesin et al. motivate the volume-preserving kernel, while Dacorogna--Moser and Teixeira provide prescribed-Jacobian and localized volume-correction context. Milnor supports the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse condition. Compact-manifold density and confidence-set results support the sampling rung, but the propagation exponent here comes from the proved scalar finite-type rigidity lemma.
prose_updates.interpretation: The two exponents answer different certified questions. The localized Hamiltonian family proves that no uniform full-class inverse modulus can improve on the lower obstruction \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). Scalar finite-type rigidity guarantees recovery for every admissible decoder at the more conservative order \(\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\). Radial incompressibility closes this gap, but no corresponding arbitrary-map coercivity theorem has yet been proved. Thus \(3/4\) is sharp for the primary radial model and a lower obstruction for the primary full class, whereas \(1/3\) is the current full-class upper exponent.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The full-class upper exponent is presently \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), obtained from scalar ratio residuals after the complete-law reduction. The desired exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) is proved only for the radial volume-preserving subclass. Symmetrizing the aligned loss does not supply the missing weighted incompressible coercivity, and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}=0\) is not used as a converse test for quotient equivalence. Any counterexample to the sharper upper bound must still arise from legal complete causal law families and respect density, smoothness, conditioning, critical-separation, and attained-order bounds.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The general contribution is a full-class bracket: lower exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) and upper exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\). The radial restricted supremum has the sharp exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\). For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the full bracket is \(c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}\), the radial rate is exactly of order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\), and the certified estimator and confidence diameter have rate \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\). The primary class uses separated critical points and the direct Hessian bound \(|r_i''(z)|\geq a_0\), without invoking a higher-smoothness quantitative-Morse theorem. Plateaus, coalescing critical points, critical submanifolds, vector-valued contrast curves, unknown-order adaptation, and the matching arbitrary-map upper bound remain outside the proved claim.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem delivers the proved full-class inverse-modulus bracket and distinguishes its sharp lower obstruction from its conservative upper guarantee.
statement_notes.gap: No cited exact-identification or Morse theorem proves the arbitrary-map incompressible inequality needed to replace the upper exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\) by \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\).
statement_notes.consumer: Learners obtain a valid uniform law-to-encoder guarantee now, while the remaining exponent gap is stated as a precise analytic target.

statement_notes.justification: The reduction records the primary full bracket, the sharp radial \(3/4\) result, direct zero-law identification, and the plateau exclusion without conflating them.
statement_notes.gap: Radial sharpness does not establish a sharp full-class rate for arbitrary bounded \(C^2\) torus diffeomorphisms.
statement_notes.consumer: Two-angle applications can distinguish the certified \(1/3\) full-class upper exponent from the sharp \(3/4\) radial exponent and lower obstruction.
